title: Pet Sematary
about: A doctor moves his family to rural Maine and learns about the burial ground beyond the pet cemetery.

Stay on the porch.How to make it400g peanuts in the shell1 tsp sea salt flakes1 jar pickled onions200g sharp cheddar1 packet crackersRoast the peanuts at 180°C for 20 minutes and salt while hot.Lay out on an old tray with pickled onions, a wedge of cheddar and crackers for the porch.Kite day picnic devilled eggsYolks whipped with mayo, mustard and relish, topped with crisp shallots, paprika and chivesHow to make itNot on tonight's cookDevilled eggs whipped with mayo, mustard and a little relish, topped with crisp shallots, paprika and chives, packed into a picnic box.Boil 8 eggs for 10 minutes, cool in iced water, peel and halve.Mash the yolks with 4 tbsp mayonnaise, 2 tsp mustard, 1 tbsp sweet pickle relish, salt and pepper until smooth.Pipe back into the whites.Thinly slice 2 shallots and fry in oil until golden and crisp, then drain.Top each egg with paprika, crisp shallots and snipped chives, and chill until the picnic.MainsLudlow baked beans with brown breadNavy beans baked 4 hours with ham hock and molasses, brown bread, coleslawHow to make it500g dried navy beans1 ham hock1 onion, halved80ml molasses2 tbsp brown sugar1 tsp English mustard1 L water1 loaf wholemeal bread1 bag coleslaw mix50g butterSoak the beans overnight in cold water, then drain.Put the beans, ham hock, onion, molasses, sugar, mustard and water in a covered dish.Bake at 150°C for 4 hours.Spread the brown bread with the butter and serve with the beans and coleslaw.Louis's Thanksgiving turkey breast roastHerb butter roasted, cornbread stuffing, mash and gravy, while the family's in ChicagoHow to make itNot on tonight's cookTurkey breast roasted with herb butter until juicy, with cornbread stuffing, buttery mash, cranberry sauce and a rich pan gravy.Heat the oven to 180°C.Rub a 1.5kg turkey breast roll with 50g butter mashed with sage, thyme and garlic and roast for 75 minutes to 70°C inside, then rest 15 minutes.Mix 300g crumbled cornbread with 1 diced onion softened in butter, chopped sage, 1 egg and 150ml stock and bake for 30 minutes alongside.Mash 1kg potatoes with butter and milk.Make gravy from the tray juices, 1 tbsp flour and 300ml stock.Serve with cranberry sauce.Something SweetRoute 15 apple crispCinnamon apples under a buttery oat crumble toppingHow to make it6 apples, sliced1 tsp cinnamon60g caster sugar1 lemon, juiced100g cold butter, cubed80g plain flour80g rolled oats80g brown sugar300ml pouring creamToss the apples with cinnamon, sugar and lemon juice in a dish.Rub the butter into the flour, oats and brown sugar and scatter over.Bake at 180°C for 40 minutes.Serve with pouring cream.Church's blueberry muffinsChurch comes back smelling wrong. Bake these anyway.How to make it300g plain flour150g caster sugar2 tsp baking powder250ml buttermilk80g butter, melted1 egg200g blueberries2 tbsp cinnamon crumble toppingMix the flour, sugar and baking powder. Stir in the buttermilk, butter and egg briefly.Fold in the blueberries and spoon into a 12-hole tin.Top with cinnamon crumble and bake at 200°C for 20 minutes.Cool in the tin for 10 minutes.To DrinkJud's porch lager and apple cider shandyLager, sparkling apple cider and lemon, for when Jud says come and have a beerHow to make it4 bottles of lager, 200ml needed per glass600ml sparkling apple cider1 lemon1 green applePut four pint glasses in the freezer for 30 minutes.Pour cold lager into each, then top slowly with chilled sparkling apple cider.Add a squeeze of lemon and a thin slice of green apple and serve straight away.Ice-cold MoxieSit on the porch with Jud.
